In Freud's dream theory, the dream as the dreamer remembers it.
In Freud's dream theory, the hidden unconscious wishes and thoughts behind a dream.
Freud's term for the unconscious operations (condensation, displacement, symbolic representation, secondary revision) that turn latent content into the manifest dream.
Thoughts and concerns from the dreamer's current waking life that appear in a dream.
The dream-work step in which a more mature part of the ego shapes the dream into a more coherent form.
Freud's 1900 model of the mind as three systems: conscious, preconscious and unconscious.
In the topographic model, mental content that can become conscious when attention is turned to it.
The illogical, timeless, wish-fulfilling mode of thought Freud placed in the unconscious, governed by the pleasure principle.
Freud's inborn tendency to avoid pain and seek pleasure by discharging tension.
Freud's learned function that tempers the pleasure principle by delaying gratification; tied to ego maturation.
The urge to keep repeating past traumatic behavior; Freud inferred the death instinct from it.
Anna O's name for recalling, with feeling, the scenes in which her symptoms began; she also called it chimney sweeping.
Freud's 1923 model of the mind as id, ego and superego, told apart by function rather than by consciousness.
Freud's later view of anxiety as an unconscious warning that mobilizes the ego's defenses against danger.
The ego's capacity to integrate varied elements into one whole; described by Nunberg in 1931.
Hartmann's term for the rearing setting in which the primary autonomous ego functions develop normally.
A masochistic giving up of one's own needs for others, satisfied only through introjection; contrasted with mature altruism.
Freud's early proposal that hysterical and obsessive-compulsive symptoms grew out of childhood sexual experiences.
In Kohut's terms, a narcissistic transference in which the analyst stands for or answers the patient's grandiose self.
In Kohut's terms, a narcissistic transference in which all strength is placed in the idealized analyst.
